title: Support Vector and Kernel Regression knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Support Vector and Kernel Regression”?
options: The method always performs better than a simple baseline, regardless of the task.
Regression predicts a numeric target. Compare predictions with a baseline, use metrics suited to the error costs, and inspect residuals rather than relying on one aggregate score.
The method proves that every prediction will be correct on all future datasets.
The method removes the need to inspect data quality or define an evaluation strategy.
questions.answer_key: Regression predicts a numeric target. Compare predictions with a baseline, use metrics suited to the error costs, and inspect residuals rather than relying on one aggregate score.
questions.explanation: The lesson frames the topic this way: Regression predicts a numeric target. Compare predictions with a baseline, use metrics suited to the error costs, and inspect residuals rather than relying on one aggregate score. The other options make unsupported guarantees.

questions.prompt: What is a sound first step when applying “Support Vector and Kernel Regression” to a new task?
options: Name the inputs, assumptions, and output for Support Vector Regression; then test it on representative data.
Tune against the final test set until the preferred metric increases.
Remove records that produce unexpected outcomes without investigating them.
Assume the default parameters are best for every dataset.
questions.answer_key: Name the inputs, assumptions, and output for Support Vector Regression; then test it on representative data.
questions.explanation: Define the input, output, assumptions, and evidence needed. For Support Vector Regression, a small representative check is more useful than blind tuning.

questions.prompt: What conclusion is appropriately cautious after trying “Support Vector and Kernel Regression”?
options: A single successful run proves fairness, robustness, and production readiness.
A higher training score alone proves generalization to unseen data.
An internal estimator score replaces domain review and operational monitoring.
A successful small example is useful evidence about that example, but generalization, risks, and limitations still need separate checks.
questions.answer_key: A successful small example is useful evidence about that example, but generalization, risks, and limitations still need separate checks.
questions.explanation: A demonstration only supports conclusions within its scope. Evaluate representative unseen cases and report limitations before production use.
